title: Scientific guards for the active v0 pilot profiles
purpose: Language-neutral scientific expectations for the three profiles in the active v0 catalogue.
rules: Build contracts from each active profile's generated positive fixture plus explicit patches.
Keep only checks that apply to profiles in the active catalogue.
Add profile-specific scientific guards as each profile is reviewed and approved.
strict_mode: The active v0 suite contains guards only; every guard must pass in Python and TypeScript.

cases.title: Identical protein-sequence contracts are exact matches
cases.why: The pilot needs a positive baseline showing that the same declared sequence contract can connect without conversion or approval.
cases.conditions: Both ports make the same complete declarations for the active protein-sequence profile.

cases.title: Different protein-sequence alphabets are incompatible
cases.why: Amino-acid and nucleotide strings do not have the same biological interpretation and cannot be treated as direct substitutes.
cases.conditions: Both ports explicitly declare their sequence alphabet and no translation step is supplied.

cases.title: Protein-sequence encoding is required
cases.why: A sequence cannot be interpreted reliably unless its encoding is declared.
cases.conditions: A contract claims the protein-sequence profile but omits the required encoding.

cases.title: Different canonicalisation methods do not directly match
cases.why: Canonical SMILES is method-dependent, so strings produced by different declared canonicalisation methods cannot be assumed identical.
cases.conditions: Both ports declare different canonicalisation methods and no normalising adapter is supplied.

cases.title: Canonical SMILES tool version is required
cases.why: The same tool can change canonical output between versions, so the method must be reproducibly identified.
cases.conditions: A contract claims the canonical-SMILES profile but omits the normalisation tool version.

cases.title: Different protein-structure coordinate systems are incompatible
cases.why: Coordinates expressed in different systems cannot be consumed as if their numerical values had the same spatial meaning.
cases.conditions: Both ports explicitly declare different coordinate systems and no conversion is supplied.

cases.title: Protein-structure origin is required
cases.why: An experimentally determined structure and a predicted structure have different provenance and limitations.
cases.conditions: A contract claims the protein-structure profile but omits whether the structure is experimental, predicted, or otherwise derived.
